card.intuition: AI is a moving label, not a technology — it names whatever computers can newly, impressively do, and the pointer has shifted from symbolic reasoning to expert systems to today's large language models. Once a technique works reliably it gets renamed 'just statistics' and the label slides to the next unsolved problem. In technical discussion, swap 'AI' for the precise part you mean: the model, the harness, the agent, or the context it was given.
card.analogy: A startup job title like 'lead visionary' that keeps migrating to whichever engineer just shipped a surprising demo — the title never refers to one fixed person, it follows the latest impressive trick.
card.time_complexity: 'AI' is a label, not a billable unit, so cost lands on whatever the word actually points at — the model provider request. Resolving the label to the concrete part (model, harness, agent) is what lets you estimate cost at all.
card.space_complexity: The word 'AI' carries no context of its own — the memory footprint lives in the pieces it stands for: the model's frozen parameters plus the context window the harness fills on every request.
when_to_use: Scoping a vague requirement like 'can AI handle the triage queue' into a model plus harness plus tools
Explaining that contradictory claims about 'AI' usually carry different timestamps
Keeping 'AI coding' as a practice label while naming the model, harness, or context underneath
gotchas: Avoid 'AI' in technical claims — name the part you mean, since a moving label makes diagnosis impossible
A claim like 'AI can't reason' may be about expert systems, image classifiers, or last month's LLM — the label hides the timestamp
